name_note: Vescimonas is a recently named genus; most genomes GTDB places here carry the NCBI name Oscillibacter, from which Vescimonas was separated.

sentences.text: Vescimonas is a genus of Gram-stain-negative, obligately anaerobic, non-spore-forming, non-motile rods isolated from human faeces, with the species Vescimonas coprocola and Vescimonas fastidiosa.
Its isolates were placed in the family Ruminococcaceae and showed 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity values lower than 96.2 % to the closely related species.
A study of gut microbiome diversity reported that, within the family Oscillospiraceae, the abundance of Vescimonas was negatively correlated with body mass index.

In a study of peninsular Malaysian populations, Vescimonas was among genera reported as more prevalent among urban individuals, while Prevotella and Cryptobacteroides were enriched in rural populations.
